content: Teplizumab has been approved for use in delaying the progression to stage 3 type 1 diabetes in individuals aged 8 years and older who are at high risk of developing the disease. This approval is based on evidence from clinical studies demonstrating its ability to slow the progression to symptomatic diabetes. In a clinical trial involving individuals at high risk for type 1 diabetes, participants were randomly assigned to receive either teplizumab or a placebo. The results of the trial showed that the median time to develop stage 3 type 1 diabetes was significantly longer in the teplizumab group, with a delay of 48.4 months compared to 24.4 months in the placebo group. Furthermore, 43% of individuals treated with teplizumab were able to delay the onset of diabetes, whereas 72% of those in the placebo group progressed to stage 3 diabetes. Eligibility for teplizumab treatment is typically determined by the presence of specific genetic markers, such as the absence of HLA-DR4, and the presence of diabetes-related autoantibodies. The most commonly reported side effects of teplizumab include rash, which occurs in approximately 73% of patients, and lymphopenia, a condition characterized by a reduced number of lymphocytes in the blood.
